title: Special Topics: Theory of LLM Reasoning
weeklyTopics: Background (2.5 weeks): Transformers architecture (Jurafsky & Martin ch. 9)
Background: Large Language Models (J&M ch. 10), proper scoring rules
Background: Model alignment, prompting, in-context learning, RLHF/PPO/GRPO/DPO (J&M ch. 12)
Background: Reasoning LLMs overview (DeepSeek R1 technical report, survey of reasoning LLMs)
Theory papers (4.5 weeks): emergent in-context learning as implicit structure induction
Theory: chain-of-thought and transformer expressiveness (serial computation, Boolean circuits)
Theory: scaling test-time compute, verifier-based vs verifier-free methods
Theory: test-time compute as meta reinforcement learning
Theory: context-enhanced learning and sample efficiency of chain-of-thought supervision
Theory: information-theoretic analysis of chain-of-thought reasoning
Theory: learning-theoretic framework for autoregressive chain-of-thought
Theory: optimal chain-of-thought length, confidence-limiting fine-tuning objectives
Theory: PAC-learnability of verifiers for chain-of-thought reasoning
Open questions: whether CoT reasoning is a distribution-dependent 'mirage', anthropomorphization of intermediate tokens, RL with minimal training data
skills: reading and critiquing ml theory papers
workloadNotes: PhD-level half-semester (7-week) special topics course requiring strong mathematical maturity and interest in LLM reasoning; structured as background reading (~2.5 weeks) followed by close reading and discussion of recent (2024-2025) machine learning theory papers on chain-of-thought and test-time compute (~4.5 weeks); no grading breakdown found in-repo.
prerequisitesText: Strong interest in reasoning and LLMs, and a high level of mathematical maturity.
textbooks: Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing (3rd ed. draft), chapters 9, 10, 12
